Tidy, glance and augment fgls fits

Source: R/broom.R
fgls-broom.Rd

Methods for the 'broom' generics (from the 'generics' package), registered when 'generics' is loaded.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'fgls'
tidy(x, conf.int = FALSE, conf.level = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'fgls'
glance(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'fgls'
augment(
  x,
  data = NULL,
  newdata = NULL,
  se_fit = FALSE,
  interval = c("none", "confidence"),
  conf.level = 0.95,
  ...
)

Arguments

x

An "fgls" object.

conf.int

Include confidence intervals.

conf.level

Confidence level.

...

Not used.

data

Data to augment: by default the model frame. It must have one row per observation used in the fit or, for a fit with na.action = na.exclude, one row per row of the original data (the excluded rows then get NA).

newdata

Optional new data; fitted values (and, if requested, standard errors and confidence limits) are added, but no residuals.

se_fit

Add the standard errors of the fitted means (.se.fit).

interval

"none" or "confidence": add confidence limits for the mean of the response (.lower, .upper) at level conf.level.

Value

A data frame (a tibble if 'tibble' is installed): one row per coefficient for tidy(), one row for glance(), one row per observation for augment() (columns .fitted, optionally .lower, .upper and .se.fit, then .resid, .innovation and, with a heteroskedasticity correction, .weight). nonexogeneity.share in glance() is NA when the share was not computed.

Examples

if (requireNamespace("broom", quietly = TRUE)) {
  fit <- serial_fgls(y ~ x, data = simulate_serial(200, seed = 1))
  broom::tidy(fit, conf.int = TRUE)
  broom::glance(fit)
  head(broom::augment(fit))
}
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>       y      x .fitted   .resid .innovation
#>   <dbl>  <dbl>   <dbl>    <dbl>       <dbl>
#> 1 2.25   1.06   2.24    0.00406      NA    
#> 2 2.08   1.77   2.94   -0.854        -0.858
#> 3 0.878 -1.17   0.0568  0.821         1.52 
#> 4 1.48  -0.690  0.524   0.951         0.281
#> 5 3.94   2.83   3.97   -0.0334       -0.810
#> 6 1.42  -0.153  1.05    0.373         0.400
